title: Chemistry and Consistency in Early Dating
keyword: chemistry and consistency in early dating
excerpt: Early dating can feel exciting. Keep chemistry and consistency in view, talk about intentions, and let attraction and information grow together.
content:
After a great first date, your mind may move quickly into the future. You can imagine the weekends, the conversations, and the life you might share.

Enjoying that excitement is allowed. You can also leave room to learn who the person is.

## Keep two kinds of information in view

Chemistry is the attraction or connection you experience. Consistency is something you observe as interactions accumulate.

Ask yourself a few ordinary questions: Do they make plans that fit both your lives? Do they do what they say they will do? Can you disagree about something small? Do they respect your pace?

You will not have every answer after two dates. "I don't know yet" is a useful answer when the relationship is new.

## Keep your existing life in the picture

Continue seeing friends and making time for your responsibilities and interests. This gives you room to enjoy dating without making a new person the center of every decision.

If you want more time together, notice whether the wish is mutual and whether the pace works for you.

## Talk about intentions

You could say: "I've enjoyed getting to know you. I'm interested in a relationship if we turn out to be a good match. What are you looking for?"

An honest difference in intentions may be disappointing. It is still valuable information.

If the answer is vague, you can ask a follow-up rather than filling in the gap yourself. If uncertainty continues, consider how long you want to remain in that arrangement.

After your next date, record one thing you enjoyed and one thing you learned. Include behavior, not just the intensity of your feelings.

The goal is to let attraction and information develop together, at a pace you can live with.
